items.position: AI-related stocks were a bubble and it has started to deflate; he is less certain than in 2005 because the technology is new, but historical patterns probably apply. Using the Buffett indicator (market cap/GDP), which through Sept 30 was far above its norm and above the dotcom peak, with AI names almost half the S&P 500, he doubts the justifications: productivity is only slightly above its 20-year average, and even if the labor share keeps falling, competition (including Chinese open-weight models at a fraction of the cost) makes it very doubtful the leaders keep the profits. Hyperscalers are priced as future Microsofts; they could be future WorldComs. The dotcom bust came in stages, and a return of the indicator to 2019 levels would erase roughly 80% of GDP in wealth (~$25 trillion). Economic effects to follow in a later post.
items.sign_basis: Explicit call that the AI equity bubble is popping, with a much larger second leg possible.

Whether air is leaving the bigger AI bubble is unknowable, but it is a 'frighteningly plausible' scenario given the circular investment structure.
